title: Molo, Hal Morento and a record that was never cut
summary: He recalls a rehearsal at Hal's barbershop for two sides, including the Peculiar Rag, which was never recorded.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Which molo was this? This is a...
Molo, that's the, I don't know whether you know the drum player, the molo the drummer?
I never met the drummer, I met the cornet player.
Yeah, but Manuel was a cornet player, I knew him. But his brother was Leonce, is that the one?
No, this was, I know his name was Molo. He was a dark and plected, big tall fella. And he played nice trombone.
And I think Sam or something. Sam was the brother, I was the drummer. Sam was the drummer, I never met him.

I played with him too, with Hal Morento. You know Hal, the piano player? Well I played, we were supposed to cut the peculiar rag on a record with that group. But Molo on drums, Hal Morento on piano, myself on trumpet, Raymond on clarinet, Philly Mill on bass. I forget who the other one fellow was, but we rehearsed at Hal's Barbershop. Hal was cutting there then, to cut the peculiar rag and the dirty rag, I believe it was in the cut, cut a record, two sides. And we never, I don't know what happened, we didn't cut the record.

Well that's a long time back too. 20s or 30s? That was the late 20s. Late 20s. Yeah. Not too late, it had been about 1925. Yeah, because I was a youngster, I must have, a youngster then. No trombone? Yeah, there must have been a trombone. I can't recall who it was, Dick. But I know Hal was in the group, Hal Morento. And I find it funny why Katz wasn't on drum, but Molo was playing drums. I remember that distinctly. And Katz and I used to bum together those days. I found it funny why Katz wasn't on drum. But I distinctly remember Molo.
I think it was Hal Morento's band.
And was it for a commercial record company?
Or were you done it? No, I don't believe, I think it just.

How I wanted those two numbers. He wanted the peculiar rag more than any of them. That's a tune you know, ain't none of these bands play. Sharky, that's the only word. And Sharky don't play it like it was written, huh? No. Uh-uh. You know, I don't know why, but, the only band I heard play it like it was written was Norman Brownlee. See, there's a piano part in there after the introduction. Uh-huh. There's a piano part in there. I never heard a piano people make it. A piano man make it. Brownlee used to make it.
Well, they can't make it right. I don't know.
